title: PLC+ — foundations
note: The instructors' release (D24): modules 1-8 and 11 are first drafts; 9, 10 and 12 come later. Challenges marked example are the machines on the Example tabs, like the exercises' machines but not the same ones (D21).

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Three rungs: one contact for Green, two in series (AND) for Amber, a normally closed contact for Red.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: Red uses a normally open contact, so it lights in Auto instead of Manual.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Rung 1: Start, or the Motor's own contact in parallel with it (the seal-in), passes power through Stop to the Motor coil. Let go of Start and the seal-in keeps the motor running. Stop is wired normally closed (TRUE until pressed), so the program checks it with a normally open contact: pressing Stop opens it and breaks the circuit.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: Rung 1 has no seal-in contact: the motor runs only while Start is held down.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Three on-delay timers in a chain, each started by the one before finishing; the last one restarts the first.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: Yellow has nothing to turn it off when red comes on, so the two are on together.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Two start/stop circuits, one per direction, each stopped by its limit switch and locked out by the other; the down rung also needs the safety eye clear.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: The down rung does not check the safety eye, so the door comes down on whatever is in the doorway.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Two latched memory tags, Filling and Draining, set and reset by the floats; the valves follow them.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: Without memory, the valves follow the high float alone: the tank chatters around 80 % and never drains.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: The metal sensor latches MetalSeen; the diverter pushes when the photo-eye sees a part and MetalSeen is set; the part leaving the eye resets it.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: The diverter pushes every part that reaches the eye, metal or plastic.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Three rungs: Ready follows the guard; Press closing needs Left hand AND Right hand AND the guard shut (three contacts in series); Guard open uses a normally closed contact (NOT).

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: The two hand buttons are side by side (OR), so the press closes with one hand on a button: the other hand could be under it.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Rung 1: PumpStart, or the pump's own contact beside it (the seal-in), through PumpStop and OverloadOK to the Pump coil. Both are wired normally closed, so normally open contacts pass power until Stop is pressed or the overload trips. Rung 2 lights the lamp.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: PumpStop is checked with a normally closed contact. The button is wired normally closed (TRUE while not pressed), so that contact is open all the time and the pump never starts. The most common mistake with Stop buttons.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Two start/stop circuits with seal-ins. Each has a normally closed contact of the other direction (the interlock), so only one can be on.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: There is no interlock: press Reverse while the motor runs forward, and both contactors are told to pull in at once.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Overheat sets a memory tag, Alarm; ResetPB AND NOT Overheat resets it. The light and the horn follow Alarm, so the alarm stays on until someone resets it.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: The light and the horn follow the temperature switch directly. The moment the oven cools, the alarm clears itself, and nobody knows it was ever too hot.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Rung 1 turns the press into a one-scan Pulse with a rising-edge contact (ONS on Allen-Bradley). Rung 2 flips the light on each Pulse.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: Without the edge, Pulse is TRUE for every scan the button is held (one scan is 10 ms), so the light flips on and off many times a press and ends up wherever it happens to stop.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Rung 1 remembers Start (RunRequest, a seal-in). Rung 2 times 3 s from RunRequest with a TON. The horn sounds while RunRequest is on and T1.Q is not; the motor runs on T1.Q. Stop drops RunRequest, which resets the timer, so every start gets the full warning.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: The timer's IN is the Start button, not RunRequest. A TON resets the moment its IN goes off, so when Start is let go the time goes back to 0: the horn sounds for ever and the motor never starts (unless Start is held for 3 s).

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Rung 1: either stair button (in parallel) starts a pulse timer (TP); its Q is on for exactly 5 s. Rung 3: DoorOpen drives an off-delay timer (TOF); its Q is on while the door is open and 4 s after it shuts.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: The stair light uses an off-delay (TOF) instead of a pulse (TP). A quick press looks right, but hold the button: the light stays on all the time it is held, and 5 s after. A pulse timer times from the press, whatever the button does.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: The heater follows its switch; an off-delay timer (TOF) on the heater keeps Q on for 5 s after it turns off; a pulse timer (TP) on Purge gives 3 s per press; the fan runs while either Q is on.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: The fan rung uses the Purge button's contact instead of the pulse timer's Q, so the fan runs only while Purge is held.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: The heater runs with Bake On, the door shut and T1 not done. T1 is a retentive timer (TONR; RTO on Allen-Bradley) whose IN is the heater: it adds up heating time, keeps it while the door is open, and only Clear (its R input) sets it back to 0.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: An ordinary TON loses its time whenever its IN goes off. Open the door at 3 s and shut it at 5 s: watch ET go back to 0, and the bake start again from the beginning. Even without the door, when the bake is done and the heater turns off, the TON resets at once: Done lights for a single scan and the heater starts another bake.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: The pump's seal-in; a retentive timer (TONR) on Pump adds up the running time over every start and keeps Q on; the Reset key in its R input clears it.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: The retentive timer has nothing in its R input. It adds up the running time, but once Service due is lit nothing can clear it: the Reset key does nothing.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: One up/down counter (CTUD): CarIn on the rung counts up, CarOut in CD counts down, ResetPB in R sets 0. QU (count at PV, 5, or more) lights Full; Spaces is lit while QU is off. A MOVE copies CV to the display.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: The counter's CD input is empty, so cars leaving are never counted: fill the car park, let a car out, and it still says Full.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: The belt's seal-in has a normally closed contact of C1.Q, so it stops when the batch is done. An up counter (CTU, PV 5) counts PartEye; Next batch in its R input clears it. A MOVE shows CV on the display.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: Nothing resets the counter: Next batch does nothing, Batch done stays lit and the belt cannot start again.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Two TONs drive each other: T1 times the on part; T1.Q starts T2, which times the off part; T2.Q resets T1, which resets T2, and round it goes. The beacon is on while T1 is timing. A counter (CTU, PV 3) counts the beacon's flashes and its Q sounds the horn; AlarmOff resets it.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: One timer resetting itself: its Q is on for a single scan (10 ms) every 0.5 s, so the beacon only blinks off for 10 ms, too short to see. A flasher needs a second timer for the off time.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: C1 counts bottles (PV 6). When it finishes, C1.Q counts one pack on C2 (PV 4), and PackReset clears C1 in the next scan, so C1.Q is a one-scan pulse per pack. C2.Q stops the belt and lights Case full; Case removed clears both.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: C1 is never cleared when a pack is done: it goes on counting 7, 8, 9 … and its Q stays on, so C2 counts just one pack and the case never fills.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: A CTU counts the parts (Reset in its R). Batch done: GE C1.CV BatchSize, so it stays lit past the size. Filling batch: GT C1.CV 0 AND LT C1.CV BatchSize.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: EQ (EQU) instead of GE for Batch done: it is lit only while the count is exactly the batch size, so one part more turns it off.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Rung 1: a down counter keeps the parts left (Refill loads 10). Rung 2: Parts low while the count is at most WarnAt (LE) AND more than 0 (GT): two compares in series. Rung 3: Bin empty at 0 or less (LE 0), so it stays lit even if Part used is pressed once too often.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: LT (less than, LES) instead of LE (less than or equal, LEQ): with Warn at 3, Parts low waits until only 2 are left. Choosing between < and <= is the most common compare mistake.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Rising-edge contacts and ADD 1 count each press; ADD gives the total; behind GT Total 0, MUL RejectCount 100 then DIV by Total gives the percentage.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: Divides before it multiplies: RejectCount / Total is 0 in whole numbers (1 / 3 = 0), so the percentage is 0 until every part is a reject.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Rung 1: a compare (GT PerBox 0) in front of DIV and MOD, so they run only when there is something to divide by. DIV keeps the whole number of boxes and drops the remainder; MOD gives that remainder. Rung 2 lights the warning when PerBox is 0.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: No check in front of DIV: dial Parts per box to 0 and the PLC stops with a math fault, every output goes off, and only Reset starts it again. Try it, then read the fault message above the rungs.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: RecipeB off: MOVE 5 to Target; on: MOVE 8. A CTU with PV Target counts the scoops; MOVE C1.CV shows the count; C1.Q lights Recipe done.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: Both MOVEs have no contact, so both run on every scan and the lower one wins: Target is always 8.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Rung 1: AcceptPB in front of MOVE, so the thumbwheel is copied only while Accept is pressed; the display keeps the number after that. Rung 2: Clear moves 0 in.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: A MOVE with no contact in front runs on every scan, so the display follows the thumbwheel and Accept does nothing. Turn the thumbwheel and watch.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Behind GE Recipe 1 and LE Recipe 4, MOVE FillTime[Recipe] to FillPT; LT 1 OR GT 4 lights BadRecipe; a normally closed BadRecipe contact in the valve's rung.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: The program this exercise starts with: every recipe fills for recipe 1's time (FillTime[1]), and nothing checks the recipe number.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Rung 1 fills the table (three MOVEs in a row). Rung 2 checks that Shift is 1 to 3 (GE and LE) and only then copies Targets[Shift] to the display. Rung 3 handles every other number. Dial 4: the light comes on and the PLC keeps running.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: No check before the index: dial 0 or 4 to 9 and the PLC stops with an index-out-of-range fault, and every output goes off. Try it, read the fault message, then press Reset.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Four steps, each a memory tag on a seal-in rung: set by the step before and the sensor that says it has finished, held by its own contact, ended by the next step or Stop. The outputs come last: the clamp is out in steps 1 to 3, the stamp down in step 2.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: Step 2 does not wait for ClampIsOut. The stamp comes down while the clamp is still moving, on a part that is not held yet.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Four steps, each a memory tag on a seal-in rung. A step starts from the step before AND the sensor that says that step has finished, and the next step ends it. The outputs come last: the gripper is closed in steps 1 and 2, the arm goes out in step 2 and back in step 4.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: Nothing ends step 1, so it stays on for the whole cycle. The gripper is told to stay closed, never lets go of the part at the far end, and the cycle stops at step 3.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Step holds the step number. Each output rung is an EQ box for its step; each move on is EQ for the step it leaves, the condition, and a MOVE of the next number. Start counts only in step 0; Stop moves 0 in from any step.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: Start's rung has no EQ box for step 0, so Start works in every step: pressed while draining, it jumps back to step 1 and fills the tank again.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Step holds the step number. Each move on is EQ for the step it leaves, its condition, and a MOVE of the next number. Each output has ONE rung: BasketDown has two EQ boxes side by side, for steps 1 and 2.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: BasketDown has two rungs, one for step 1 and one for step 2. The PLC runs them in order, so in step 1 the second rung turns the coil off again: the basket never goes down, and the washer waits in step 1 for ever.

programs.title: Written as an SFC
programs.note: The same washer written as a Sequential Function Chart would be drawn: one BOOL per step (S0 to S4), S0 the initial step, so its tag starts TRUE. Each step's rung starts it from the step before AND the transition's condition, and the next step ends it. The actions (outputs and timers) come last. The last five rungs show the active step on the Step display.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: State holds the state number. Each move is a rung: EQ for the state it leaves, its condition, MOVE the new number. The move to Stopped has no EQ (it comes from every state) and runs after the others. Reset goes to Closing, so the gate ends closed.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: Reset moves straight to Closed (0). The program now believes the gate is closed while it is still half open, and nothing will close it.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: State holds the state number. The leak alarm (8) is a state of its own: entered from any state, left only by Alarm reset with the floor dry, and then to Draining, so the tank is emptied before it is used again. Stop goes back to Idle, but not out of the alarm.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: There is no leak state: the leak only holds the valves shut while the floor is wet. When it dries, the tank carries on filling by itself and the horn stops, and nobody needs to look at the leak.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: FIXED: the bell has one coil, on rung 3, with the two buttons side by side (OR). Either button rings it.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: A double coil: rungs 2 and 4 both write Bell. Press the front button: rung 2 turns Bell on, and rung 4, later in the same scan, turns it off again. The Front light comes on, but the bell never rings from the front door.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: The horn has one coil, on rung 4, with the two faults side by side (OR).

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: Rungs 3 and 5 both write Horn (a double coil). Too hot: rung 3 turns the horn on and rung 5, later in the same scan, turns it off again, so the horn sounds only for low oil.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: FIXED: each rung's seal-in contact reads its own coil's tag: Fan on rung 1, WorkLight on rung 2.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: Rung 2 was copied from rung 1 and its seal-in contact still reads Fan. So the light stays on only while Light on is held, and comes on by itself whenever the fan runs.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Each pump's seal-in contact reads its own coil: Pump1 on rung 1, Pump2 on rung 2.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: Rung 2's seal-in contact reads Pump1, not Pump2: pump 2 runs only while its Start is held, and starts by itself whenever pump 1 runs.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: FIXED: two timing jobs, two timers. T1 times the wash (rung 2) and T2 the rinse (rung 4), and rung 3 reads T2.Q to end the rinse.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: Rungs 2 and 4 both use the timer T1. Rung 2 starts it, and rung 4, with no power, resets it in the same scan, every scan. T1's time never gets past 0, so the wash never ends.

programs.title: Works
programs.note: Two timing jobs, two timers: T1 times the warning and T2 the mixing.

programs.title: A common mistake
programs.note: Rungs 2 and 5 both use T1. While the horn sounds, rung 5 has no power and resets T1 in every scan, so the warning time never runs out.
